intents.intent: Orient / 'what do I have here' open-ended look
intents.clinical_purpose: Clinician opens a case and wants a quick read of what is loaded and what to do next, without committing to a pipeline.
example_phrasings: what's going on with this recording
intents.current_risk: System prompt line 69 guards against silently running the whole pipeline, but a weak model still tends to either over-run detection or under-act (pure prose). Behavior is not differentiated by how far the case has progressed.

behavior_by_state.S0: Explain no recording is loaded; offer to open one (recording.open). Do not fabricate.
behavior_by_state.S1: get_ui_state + recording.inspect_metadata; summarize fs/duration/channels; propose ROI/QC as next step. Do NOT auto-run detection.
behavior_by_state.S2: Note a prepared copy exists; summarize prep; propose detection as next step.
behavior_by_state.S3: Surface existing run(s) via runs_detail; summarize event counts/top channels from context; offer rank/classify/review. Do NOT re-detect.
behavior_by_state.S4: Summarize kept-vs-artifact; offer review of real candidates.
behavior_by_state.S5: Summarize review progress (accepted/remaining); offer to continue review or export.

intents.intent: Inspect recording metadata (fs, duration, channels, filters, line freq)
intents.clinical_purpose: Confirm the recording is analyzable and band-appropriate before any compute.
example_phrasings: is the sampling rate too low?
intents.current_risk: System prompt line 47 fixed the refusal misfire; low risk now. Minor: may print raw paths against the no-paths rule.

behavior_by_state.S0: No recording — say so; offer to open one.
behavior_by_state.S1: recording.inspect_metadata / pyhfo_get_recording_info; report fs, duration, channels, line freq.
behavior_by_state.S2: Same; may also note the prepared copy's parameters.
behavior_by_state.S3: Same; metadata is unchanged by detection.

intents.intent: Nyquist / band feasibility check ('can I even do ripples on this?')
intents.clinical_purpose: Decide whether the sampling rate supports the intended HFO/ripple/fast-ripple band before wasting a run.
example_phrasings: can I detect ripples on this?
is 1000 Hz enough for fast ripples?
is the fs high enough for HFOs
这个频率够不够做高频
intents.current_risk: Agent may answer from metadata fs alone without computing the spectral/Nyquist evidence, or may not connect 'fast ripple needs >=1024 Hz' to the requested band.

behavior_by_state.S0: No recording — explain it needs one loaded.
behavior_by_state.S1: compute_spectral_profile (or read fs) and state Nyquist vs the target band (ripple 80-250 needs fs>=~526; fast ripple 250-500 needs fs>=~1052).
behavior_by_state.S2: Same, using the prepared copy's resample rate if it changed fs.
behavior_by_state.S3: Same; can also note the band the existing run used.

intents.intent: Infer / select the real brain-signal ROI (exclude EKG/EOG/EMG/AUX)
intents.clinical_purpose: Restrict analysis to true intracranial brain channels so QC and detection aren't contaminated by physiologic/aux channels.
example_phrasings: which channels are real brain channels
exclude the EKG and aux channels
intents.current_risk: Low. May conflate ROI selection with QC; should run ROI first.

behavior_by_state.S1: recording.infer_roi; report included/excluded/uncertain channels with reasons.
behavior_by_state.S2: Same; note that prep may have already dropped some channels.
behavior_by_state.S3: Same; ROI is independent of runs.

intents.intent: Run channel QC / find bad/flat/noisy channels
intents.clinical_purpose: Identify technical bad channels (flat, saturated, NaN, amplitude outliers) before detection so they don't generate spurious events.
intents.current_risk: Agent may call BOTH run_qc and compute_spectral_profile though they trigger the same 3-step pass (system prompt line 37 and COMMAND_USAGE warn against this); may report QC numbers without actually running the tool (anti-fabrication rule covers this).

behavior_by_state.S1: analysis.run_qc (one call, not also spectral); report flat/noisy/outlier candidates as technical QC, not pathology.
behavior_by_state.S2: Same; note prep already handled some bad channels.
behavior_by_state.S3: Same; QC is independent of detection.

intents.intent: Spectral profile / line-noise check
intents.clinical_purpose: Quantify line noise (50/60 Hz), band power, and confirm the recommended HFO band from signal evidence.
intents.current_risk: Same dual-trigger issue as QC-01 (run_qc and compute_spectral_profile are the same pass). Line-noise number must come from the tool, not be assumed as 60 Hz.

behavior_by_state.S1: compute_spectral_profile (one call); report line-noise candidate and recommended band.
behavior_by_state.S2: Same; note if prep already notched.
behavior_by_state.S3: Same.

intents.intent: SET detector/preprocessing parameters WITHOUT running (filter band, notch, resample, n_jobs, channel drops)
intents.clinical_purpose: Configure the Prepare panel controls so the clinician can review them before committing compute.
example_phrasings: set the band to fp 80 fs 250
intents.current_risk: This was the original misroute bug (now fixed): 'set notch' previously routed into pyhfo_prepare_recording (heavy run) or analysis.prepare_recording. Fix shipped via de-magnetized prepare desc + COMMAND_USAGE + system-prompt steer. Residual risk: model may still emit a prepare run for a bare param-set, or use wrong payload keys (must be filter.fp/filter.fs/line_noise_notch_hz, not 'filtered').

behavior_by_state.S0: No recording — set_parameters requires a recording; explain or offer to open one first.
behavior_by_state.S1: detection.set_parameters (instant view-write); confirm the controls now show the values. Run nothing.
behavior_by_state.S2: Same; updating controls does not invalidate the prepared copy until a new prepare runs.
behavior_by_state.S3: Same; setting params does not affect existing runs.

intents.intent: Actually CLEAN / PREPARE the recording (execute preprocessing, write a prepared copy)
intents.clinical_purpose: Produce a reproducible cleaned/notched/resampled artifact to detect on.
example_phrasings: notch and filter it then save
apply the notch and bandpass for real
intents.current_risk: Must be distinguished from PARAM-01: only an explicit 'clean/prepare/produce a copy' should EXECUTE. Confirm-gated compute; agent must say 'staged for Apply' not 'done' until UI confirms (system prompt line 34). Re-preparing when a prepared copy already exists wastes work.

behavior_by_state.S1: analysis.prepare_recording (compute, confirm-gated); say staged for Apply; report the prep recipe in plain words.
behavior_by_state.S2: A prepared copy already exists — confirm whether they want to RE-prepare with new params (don't silently redo); otherwise point to the existing prep.
behavior_by_state.S3: Re-preparing would orphan existing runs — warn and confirm intent before re-prepping.
behavior_by_state.S4: Same warning; re-prep invalidates classified runs.
behavior_by_state.S5: Same; strong warning that re-prep discards downstream review.

intents.intent: Detect ripples specifically (ripple band 80-250 Hz) — THE STATE-DEPENDENT TEMPLATE
intents.clinical_purpose: Surface ripple-band HFOs (80-250 Hz), the clinically meaningful interictal biomarker, across channels then rank/show them.
intents.current_risk: TWO real risks. (1) BAND: there is no 'ripple' biomarker — enum is only HFO/Spindle/Spike, so 'ripple' must be encoded as filter {fp:80,fs:250}; the smoke-test default fs=min(500,0.95*Nyquist) and the 'generic HFO 80-500' note bias a weak model toward a broadband 80-500 run that is NOT ripple-specific. (2) STATE: SKILL.md line 30 treats 'I want all ripples' as an UNCONDITIONAL detection.run — it does NOT check for an existing run first. So in S3+ the agent likely RE-DETECTS instead of surfacing existing ripples. The 'don't re-detect' rule only fires for 'most active channel / where are the HFOs' phrasings, not for the bare 'I want all ripples'.

behavior_by_state.S0: No recording — explain it must be loaded first; offer recording.open.
behavior_by_state.S1: Run ripple detection: detection.run with biomarker:HFO, filter:{fp:80,fs:250}, detector:STE, scope:all, all_channels:true, n_jobs:1 (Nyquist-safe). After completion, rank/show channels. Confirm-gated.
behavior_by_state.S2: Same as S1 but detect on the prepared copy.
behavior_by_state.S3: Do NOT re-detect. get_ui_state -> if a ripple-band (or HFO) run already exists, surface it: rank_candidates + focus_top_candidate_channel / focus_hotspot_channels. Only run a NEW detection if the existing run used a different band (e.g. fast-ripple only) or the user explicitly asks to re-run.
behavior_by_state.S4: Surface the existing (classified) ripples; prefer kept/real events; rank/show. No re-detection.
behavior_by_state.S5: Surface ripples within the run under review; respect accepted/annotated state; rank/show, no re-detection.

intents.intent: Detect fast ripples specifically (250-500 Hz)
intents.clinical_purpose: Surface fast-ripple-band HFOs (250-500 Hz), a more specific epileptogenicity marker than ripples.
example_phrasings: I want fast ripples not ripples
intents.current_risk: Requires fs>=~1052 Hz (Nyquist) — agent may run on insufficient fs and silently get 0 events. Same no-distinct-biomarker issue: fast ripple = filter {fp:250,fs:500} on biomarker HFO. Same state-unawareness: may re-detect in S3.

behavior_by_state.S1: Check Nyquist; if fs supports 500 Hz, detection.run biomarker:HFO filter:{fp:250,fs:500}; else explain fs too low. Rank/show after.
behavior_by_state.S2: Same on prepared copy (check resample didn't drop fs below Nyquist).
behavior_by_state.S3: If a fast-ripple run exists, surface it (no re-detect); if only a ripple/broadband run exists, a new FR-band run is justified.
behavior_by_state.S4: Surface existing FR run, prefer kept events.

intents.intent: Detect HFOs (generic / broadband 80-500)
intents.clinical_purpose: Surface all high-frequency oscillations (ripples + fast ripples) when the clinician wants the broad HFO picture.
intents.current_risk: Conversely to DET-01, a bare 'HFO' should use the broad 80-500 band — risk is the model narrowing it to 80-250. State-unaware re-detection in S3.

behavior_by_state.S1: detection.run biomarker:HFO, broad band 80-500 (clamped to Nyquist), STE, all channels. Rank/show after.
behavior_by_state.S3: If an HFO run exists, surface/rank it (no re-detect) unless the user explicitly wants a fresh run.
behavior_by_state.S4: Surface classified HFOs, prefer kept events.

intents.intent: Detect spikes (epileptiform spikes)
intents.clinical_purpose: Surface interictal epileptiform spikes as candidate evidence.
intents.current_risk: Default detector for Spike differs (RMS/LL vs STE for HFO); model may apply HFO band to a spike run. State-unaware re-detection in S3.

behavior_by_state.S1: detection.run biomarker:Spike with a spike-appropriate detector. Rank/show after.
behavior_by_state.S3: If a spike run exists, surface/rank it (no re-detect).

intents.intent: Detect spindles (sleep spindles)
intents.clinical_purpose: Surface sleep spindles (e.g. for sleep-staged analysis).
intents.current_risk: YASA availability must be checked; LSM needs a param file. Model may default to STE (an HFO detector) for a spindle request. State-unaware re-detection in S3.

behavior_by_state.S1: Check detector availability; detection.run biomarker:Spindle with YASA or MOLLE/A7 fallback. Rank/show.
behavior_by_state.S3: If a spindle run exists, surface it (no re-detect).

intents.intent: Detect with explicit detector/parameter ('use STE with RMS=2', 'MNI detector')
intents.clinical_purpose: Run a specific detector with clinician-supplied thresholds for protocol reproducibility.
intents.current_risk: 'RMS = 2 detect STE' must keep detector=STE with detector_params:{rms_thres:2}, NOT switch to the RMS detector (SKILL.md line 29 covers this but a weak model conflates them). Must preserve explicit user params, not fall back to defaults (SKILL.md step 2).

behavior_by_state.S1: detection.run with the named detector + detector_params, preserving the user's values.
behavior_by_state.S3: A NEW parameterized run is usually legitimate here (different params) — but confirm it's a new run vs. operating on the existing one if ambiguous.

intents.intent: Recommend a detector plan ('what detector / settings should I use')
intents.clinical_purpose: Get a signal-evidence-based detector + filter recommendation before committing compute.
example_phrasings: how should I detect HFOs here
intents.current_risk: Recent fix (commit fa5d924): detection.plan now recommends a real plan instead of running ROI/QC/spectral. Residual: model may jump straight to detection.run instead of planning when asked to plan.

behavior_by_state.S1: detection.plan; present recommended detector/band/n_jobs/warnings. Do not run.
behavior_by_state.S3: Can recommend a refinement plan vs the existing run.

intents.intent: Rank candidate channels ('which channels matter / have the most events')
intents.clinical_purpose: Turn detected events into a ranked channel list — the core 'where is the activity' answer.
example_phrasings: which channels have the most events
intents.current_risk: If no run exists, ranking is impossible — agent must explain detection is needed first, not fabricate a ranking (anti-fabrication rule). Must not present ranked channels as SOZ.

behavior_by_state.S1: No run yet — explain detection must run first; offer to run it. Do NOT fabricate a ranking.
behavior_by_state.S3: detection.rank_candidates on the existing run; report ranked channels + rates as research candidates. No re-detection.
behavior_by_state.S4: Rank using kept (real) events; note artifact-rejected counts.
behavior_by_state.S5: Rank within the run under review; reflect accepted/annotated state.

intents.intent: Show / focus the single most active channel
intents.clinical_purpose: Jump the waveform to the channel with the most candidate events for visual inspection.
example_phrasings: show me the channel with the most HFO
intents.current_risk: This IS the phrasing the 'don't re-detect, surface' rule explicitly covers (SKILL.md step 7, system prompt line 38). Lower risk than DET-01. Risk only if no run exists and model re-detects instead of explaining.

behavior_by_state.S1: No run — explain detection must run first; offer to run.
behavior_by_state.S3: detection.focus_top_candidate_channel {biomarker:HFO, duration_seconds:2}. View-only, no re-detect.

intents.intent: Show / focus the top-N hotspot channels
intents.clinical_purpose: Lay out the several most event-dense channels together for comparison.
intents.current_risk: Same as LOC-02 — covered by the surface-existing rule. Risk if no run.

behavior_by_state.S1: No run — explain.
behavior_by_state.S3: waveform.focus_hotspot_channels {biomarker:HFO, top_n:8, duration_seconds:4}. View-only.

intents.intent: Classify events real-vs-artifact / remove artifacts
intents.clinical_purpose: Use the PyHFO artifact/spike/eHFO classifier to separate real biomarker events from artifacts.
intents.current_risk: eeg-classification skill correctly branches (fresh vs existing run, 'do not re-run the detector when a run already exists'). Residual: 'turn on the spike sub-classifier' could mis-route classification.run (compute) over classification.set_parameters (view) — the US-003 risk-tie-break addresses this but it's a known soft spot. Classification needs a SAVED session file, not a bare run id.

behavior_by_state.S2: Same — still no detection run to classify.

behavior_by_state.S5: Classify/re-classify within the run under review; preserve human annotations.

intents.clinical_purpose: Move the trace to a specific time or window for visual inspection.
intents.current_risk: US-005 fixed: 'go to 30 seconds' previously tied to waveform.center_event (no COMMAND_USAGE). Also commit ec3373e: now rejects non-numeric start/duration instead of jumping to 0s. Residual: needs a recording loaded.

behavior_by_state.S3: Same.

intents.clinical_purpose: Bring a clinician-named electrode into view.

The current binary 'run exists -> don't re-detect' rule has no carve-out and could wrongly block a legitimate iteration.

gaps.detail: The flagship gap: a bare 'I want all ripples' / 'find the ripples' / 'detect all HFOs' is hardcoded as an UNCONDITIONAL detection.run in pyhfo-detection/SKILL.md line 30 and COMMAND_USAGE['detection.run']. Neither instructs a get_ui_state runs_detail check first. So in S3-S5 (a run already exists) the agent re-detects instead of surfacing/ranking the existing ripples — exactly the product-owner seed insight. The 'don't re-detect' rule (system prompt line 46, SKILL step 7) only triggers for show/rank/focus phrasings ('most active channel', 'where are the HFOs'), NOT for the detect-verb 'I want all ripples'.

There is no distinct 'ripple' or 'fast ripple' biomarker — the biomarker enum is only ['HFO','Spindle','Spike'] (pyhfo_tools.py line 423). 'Ripple' = filter {fp:80,fs:250} layered on biomarker:HFO. The defaults fight the seed insight: pyhfo_detect_events smoke-test default is fs=min(500,0.95*Nyquist) (~80-500) and the skill/COMMAND_USAGE both repeat 'ripples AND fast ripples are HFOs' + 'generic HFO 80-500'. A weak model easily runs a broadband 80-500 pass for a 'ripples' request, silently widening the band beyond 80-250.

Fast-ripple (250-500 Hz) requests have no Nyquist precondition in the skill text and no distinct biomarker. On a <=1024 Hz recording an FR-band run silently yields 0 events (the known fs<Nyquist silent-failure class, memory note ieeg-fs-nyquist-detection-guard). The agent isn't told to gate DET-02 on fs>=~1052 Hz.

S2 (prepared-but-not-detected) is under-specified everywhere. No intent or skill text tells the agent that after PREP-01, detection should run on the PREPARED copy, nor how 'I want all ripples' in S2 differs from S1 (it should detect, but on the prepared artifact). The state matrix collapses S1 and S2.

The ITER-01 case (deliberate re-run with new params in S3+) is the legitimate exception to 'don't re-detect', but no skill text distinguishes it from accidental re-detection. The current binary 'run exists -> don't re-detect' rule has no carve-out for an explicit 'run it again with threshold X', risking the agent refusing a legitimate iteration.

Migrated/newer capabilities — detection.create_consensus_run, review.group_overlaps, project.save/open — rely entirely on SEARCH_KEYWORDS substring matching and are not mentioned in the skills. Clinician phrasings ('combine the runs', 'group simultaneous events', 'resume the case') may not surface them; the model has no skill-level steer toward them.

search_tools is a substring keyword ranker (progress.txt learnings): short filler tokens false-match TYPE names (the 'as'->'clASSification' bug) and generic words inside a type name win +3 type-match ties. Although de-authoritative now (browse hint only per the set-params memory note), a weak model that still trusts the search top-1 can misroute. Selftest historically only checked top-5 membership, hiding wrong top-1.

SOZ overreach vs over-refusal (SAFE-01) is a documented two-sided failure: the refusal-guard has misfired on ordinary 'which channels matter' (system prompt line 47 added to counter it), while presenting ranked candidates AS the SOZ violates the research-only contract (system prompt lines 18-19). There is no explicit intent-level template telling the agent to ANSWER the signal question while DECLINING the clinical-localization claim.

annotate->compute misroute (US-001): 'label this event as an artifact' ranked classification.run (a compute run) over events.stage_annotation due to substring matching of 'as'. Fixed via stopwords, but it is the highest-severity class (a review annotation becoming a re-classification compute) and is only guarded structurally, not by an intent-aware router.

LOC-01 (rank candidates) and CLS-01 (classify) in S0/S1/S2 (no run) must explain detection-first and NOT fabricate a ranking/classification. The anti-fabrication rule covers numbers, but there is no explicit per-state instruction that 'rank/classify with no run' returns a guidance response rather than an empty or invented one.

Many intents are confirm-gated writes whose 'staged vs done' honesty depends on autonomy level (system prompt line 34, memory note ieeg-agent-hitl-autonomy). Across states, the agent's reporting of staged/started/done is not state- or autonomy-tested for most commands — per the memory notes only set_parameters and detection.run have explicit live verification today.

recommended_fixes.change: In pyhfo-detection/SKILL.md step 5, make 'I want all ripples / find the ripples / detect all HFOs' STATE-DEPENDENT: prepend a mandatory get_ui_state runs_detail check. If a run with a matching biomarker/band already exists -> do NOT detection.run; instead rank_candidates + focus_top_candidate_channel/focus_hotspot_channels (surface existing). Only stage detection.run when NO matching run exists (S1/S2) OR the user explicitly asks to re-run/iterate (ITER-01). Use the existing ripple example as the template and state the S0/S1 vs S3 branch explicitly.

In COMMAND_USAGE['detection.run'] (ui_mcp/mcp_server.py), add the state branch in the same words as the skill: 'If get_ui_state shows a matching run already exists, do NOT re-run — surface it with detection.focus_top_candidate_channel / waveform.focus_hotspot_channels / detection.rank_candidates.' Keep it adjacent to the existing 'never ask what ripples means' line so the model sees both together.

Resolve the ripple-band ambiguity in pyhfo-detection/SKILL.md and COMMAND_USAGE: state crisply that 'ripple(s)' = filter {fp:80,fs:250} ALWAYS (not 80-500), 'fast ripple(s)' = {fp:250,fs:500}, and only a bare 'HFO/high-frequency' with no ripple/FR qualifier uses the broad 80-500. Remove the band-blurring 'ripples AND fast ripples are HFOs' phrasing from the line that sets the filter so the default for the word 'ripple' is unambiguously the 80-250 band.

Add a Nyquist precondition to DET-02 (fast ripples) in pyhfo-detection/SKILL.md: before staging an FR-band ({fp:250,fs:500}) run, confirm fs >= ~1052 Hz; if not, explain the recording can't support the fast-ripple band rather than running it to 0 events. Mirror the existing ripple-band Nyquist guidance.

Generalize the 'don't re-detect' rule (line 46) from the current show/rank phrasings to ALL detect-verb requests when a matching run exists, with an explicit carve-out for deliberate iteration ('re-run with threshold X', 'try again') which IS a legitimate new run. State the decision as: run exists + same intent -> surface; run exists + new params/explicit re-run -> new run; no run -> detect.

Add explicit S2 handling: in pyhfo-detection and eeg-preprocessing skills, state that once a prepared copy exists, detection should run on the prepared artifact, and a 'detect ripples' in S2 still detects (on the prepared copy) — distinguishing S1 (raw) from S2 (prepared) so the state matrix doesn't collapse them.

Add a SAFE-01 template to the safety contract: for SOZ/resection/ground-truth requests, ANSWER the underlying signal question (offer/return ranked candidate channels as research evidence) while explicitly DECLINING to name a SOZ or surgical target — neither refuse outright (over-refusal) nor present candidates as the SOZ (overreach). This codifies the two-sided failure the refusal-guard note describes.

Improve discoverability of migrated/newer commands (detection.create_consensus_run, review.group_overlaps, project.save/open) by adding a one-line mention in the relevant skills (eeg-result-interpretation for consensus/group, plus a project-lifecycle note) so the model knows they exist rather than relying solely on SEARCH_KEYWORDS substring matches.

Add a per-state 'no run yet' guidance line to detection.rank_candidates and classification.run COMMAND_USAGE/skills: when no matching run exists, return a 'detection must run first' guidance response and do NOT fabricate a ranking/classification — making the S0/S1/S2 behavior explicit rather than implicit in the anti-fabrication rule.

Add the state-dependent intents (ripples S1-vs-S3, fast-ripple Nyquist gate, annotate-vs-classify, SOZ answer-vs-decline, iterate-vs-resurface) to the test matrix as paired S1/S3/S5 fixtures, since the memory notes show only set_parameters and detection.run have explicit per-state live verification today. Build the matrix off the behavior_by_state column of this catalog.

summary: This catalog consolidates the clinical, capability, and state lenses into 35 de-duplicated clinician intents spanning the full iEEG co-pilot workflow (inspect, ROI, QC/spectral, parameter-set vs prepare, detect, localize/rank, classify, navigate, review, annotate, run-management, compare/consensus, accept, export, project, batch, safety, meta, iterate), each grounded in the real 38-command emit_ui_command catalog (desktop/src/features/agent/uiCommands.ts), the COMMAND_USAGE/SEARCH_KEYWORDS router (ui_mcp/mcp_server.py), the 13 pyhfo_* backend tools, and the domain skills. Every intent carries explicit behavior_by_state across S0-S5. The single biggest theme is the product owner's seed insight: 'I want all ripples' is state-dependent, but the code today treats it as an unconditional detection.run (no get_ui_state precondition), so in S3+ the agent re-detects instead of surfacing/ranking existing ripples — the surface-existing rule only fires for show/rank phrasings, not the bare detect-verb. The second theme is a band-parameter trap: there is no distinct 'ripple' biomarker (enum is HFO/Spindle/Spike), so 'ripple' must be encoded as filter {fp:80,fs:250}, yet the defaults and the 'ripples AND fast ripples are HFOs / generic HFO 80-500' phrasing bias the model toward a broadband 80-500 run that is not ripple-specific; fast-ripple requests additionally lack a Nyquist gate and silently yield 0 events on <=1024 Hz data. The third theme is two-sided safety (SOZ overreach vs documented over-refusal) plus the structural router misroutes already partly fixed (annotate->classify via the 'as'->clASSification substring bug, set-params->prepare). Recommended fixes are prioritized: P0 = make the ripple intent state-branched in both the skill and COMMAND_USAGE and disambiguate the ripple band to a hard 80-250; P1 = generalize the no-re-detect rule with an explicit iterate carve-out, add the fast-ripple Nyquist gate, separate S1-from-S2, and add a SOZ answer-while-declining template; P2 = discoverability for migrated commands and a paired S1/S3/S5 test matrix built off the behavior_by_state column.
